# Contributing

Figma: [Contributing](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-877)

How to propose, build and ship changes to Syntropy without breaking it - the rules, the workflow, and the quality bar every contribution meets.

## Before you start

Syntropy is a shared, published library - a change here ripples into every Safqah screen and into the Flutter codebase. So contributions follow a deliberate process. Read Getting Started first, then these rules.

- Check it doesn’t already exist. Search the Assets panel and the component pages before building anything new.
- One change, one purpose. Keep each addition or edit scoped and reviewable.

## The golden rules (non-negotiable)

Every contribution must satisfy all of these - they are what keep the system coherent and auditable.

- Bind everything to variables. Colour, type, spacing, radius and elevation reference Primitive / Semantic tokens - never raw hex or numbers.
- Build atoms → molecules → organisms. Compose from existing pieces; never inline a big one-off. Reuse the real Button, Tag, Icon - don’t fake them.
- Ship LTR and RTL. Every text-bearing component needs both directions, properly mirrored - not just flipped.
- Use the Syntropy icon library. Import glyphs from the published Icons file - never createNodeFromSvg custom icons or other icon packs.
- Name to the convention, and document it. An undocumented or off-convention component is not done.

## Adding a new component

The end-to-end flow for a brand-new component:

- 1 · Propose - confirm the need, check for overlap, and note the states, variants and both directions it will need.
- 2 · Decompose - list the atoms, then molecules, then the organism. Build bottom-up.
- 3 · Build with tokens - bind every paint, size and radius as you go; never “fix it later”.
- 4 · Variants & properties - combine as a variant set; add boolean / text / instance-swap properties with proper names.
- 5 · Add RTL - build the RTL direction fresh (mirroring layout and icons), not by flipping the LTR one.
- 6 · Move to its page - create the NNx. Name page in the right family and add labelled reference frames.
- 7 · Document - build the Documentation page from the Library Internals templates.
- 8 · Audit & publish - zero unbound paints, then publish the library and log it in the Changelog.

## Changing an existing component

Edits to a live component reach every instance across the product. Change carefully:

- Prefer additive changes - a new variant or property over a rename or removal.
- Renaming a variant option breaks instances (re-select is required). Only do it when the old name is genuinely wrong - and note it in the Changelog.
- Never delete a published component outright - move it to Deprecated v1 and leave a pointer to its replacement.
- Re-run the audit, re-publish, and log the change with a migration note if it’s breaking.

## Naming conventions

- Pages - NN‹letter›. Name (e.g. 02a. Button), grouped under the coloured family dividers.
- Components - PascalCase (SegmentedControl, CardDeal, IssuanceStatusBadge).
- Variant properties - Title Case that matches what the variant renders (Status = Written Off, not WrittenOff).
- Icons - Icon / kebab-case-name (Icon / wallet-add), single slash with spaces.
- Tokens - reference variables by name; never hard-code the value.

## Documentation requirements

A component isn’t done until it’s documented. Every component page carries three things:

- A Page Header - title, one-line description, status, and 2–3 resource links.
- A Documentation page built from the Library Internals templates - Overview, Anatomy, States, Direction (LTR / RTL), Tokens, Accessibility, Code Reference, Usage do/don’t, Resources.
- A reference / matrix frame showing every variant, labelled.

## Definition of Done (checklist)

Before you publish, all of these are true:

- ☐  Every paint, size, radius and text style binds to a variable - audit passes with zero raw values.
- ☐  Both LTR and RTL exist and are correctly mirrored.
- ☐  Variants and properties are named to the convention.
- ☐  Uses real Syntropy icons and real sub-components - no fakes, no custom SVG icons.
- ☐  Meets accessibility: 3:1 non-text contrast, visible focus, minimum target size, ARIA roles noted in the doc.
- ☐  A Documentation page and a labelled reference frame exist.
- ☐  Component description and status are set.

## Publishing & versioning

Shipping a change:

- Publish the library from Figma with a clear message describing the change.
- Log it in the Changelog - what changed, why, and any migration note.
- Follow semver intent: additive = minor; breaking (renames / removals) = major, with a deprecation path.
- Coordinate breaking changes with engineering - the library is the design ↔ Flutter contract.
